payload.words: A Goal's stop and its land are two events: a stop ends the runs, and the owner's land ends the Goal as a fixed snapshot that later Goals build on.

lines.text: After a Goal reaches a stop, the owner lands it with one act that hyp status prints. The act records one land event in the log, which names the stop it ends, whether or not the change was merged. A land by another role, or on a Goal with no stop, is refused.
hyp status shows a stop as an event: which stop, the act that caused it, and when.

A landed Goal prints the record of its decision, the PR body or with no select the table of outputs, in hyp status G and in the land act's return; hyp status for every Goal prints only its state block.
After a select, hyp status shows the Goal waiting for the owner, and prints the land line among the owner's acts.
A landed Goal is fixed: hyp refuses place, run, select and a second land on it.
hyp add goal --from G is refused unless G is landed.
The glossary and the spec describe land as the owner's event that ends a Goal, not as a check of a commit, and say what the snapshot is, when it is read and what for.
A selected Goal that is not landed still refuses place, run and a second select.
A log written before land existed, in which a Goal cites a Goal that is not landed, replays with nothing refused.

lines.text: When a commit's spec holds a model, select refuses it if a rule the model checks is named by no switch config, or if it holds no chart, and the refusal names each such rule or the missing chart.
The select report shows the Goal's chart, so the owner reads it in the PR without the runner pasting it.

A user of hyp in another repository can have the grill write a Goal's model, with one switch per cheap wrong build, each tried as a patch with hyp try --worktree, and its chart, with what hyp ships and the tools it names and no prompt written by hand.
A commit whose spec folder holds no model is selected as before.

payload.words: The owner can put a selected Goal back to open with unselect, so a re-grill or a recheck after main moves happens inside the same Goal.

lines.text: After the owner unselects a selected Goal, the Goal is open again: the grill may place, the runner may run, and a new select is recorded.
After an unselect the budget starts again at 0 of 3, and H0's row and the old candidate's row keep their live cells.
unselect is refused, exit 1, on a landed Goal, on a Goal that is not selected, and by any actor or role but the owner who added the Goal.

After an unselect, a runner's select is refused until a run records a cell for an example version or a row that was not run before the unselect; a rerun of the same example version on the same row does not count. The owner may select at any time.
A Goal that was never unselected keeps the state, stop and allowed acts it has today.

payload.words: The statechart tool, not the grill, says which rules each variant breaks and which examples each variant would meet; the grill tries what the tool predicts, and only a tried variant that meets every example reaches the owner, as one plain question.

lines.text: The statechart tool writes one variant config per variant that lists exactly the rules that variant breaks, and prints each rule that no variant breaks as not shown to fail.
For each example of a Goal, the tool prints a walk of the model whose last state prints what meets the example's floors and ceilings, or says that no walk of the model does.

For each example and each variant, the tool prints whether the example is met under that variant, from the model alone and with no patch, and for each variant it prints the examples that separate it, or none.

The report holds a rules table (rule, source, broken by, an example sees it break), an examples by variants table with predicted and tried cells and a separated-by row, and one part for each variant that no example separates, naming its rules, the step no example takes and the two prints; when the grill gives the tool the verdicts `hyp try --worktree` printed on a variant's patch, each tried cell sits beside its prediction and each cell where they differ is named.
Each rule of the model names its source: a line of the Goal, an owner decision, or model only. The tool lists each rule with no source and each line of the Goal that no rule names.

A user of hyp in another repository can have the grill draft the model after the owner consents to the words and lines and before the examples are final, try with `hyp try --worktree` each variant the tool predicts to meet every example and one predicted-fail example of each other variant, and fix the model, not an example, where a try differs from its prediction, saying so in one line of the hand-off.

A user of hyp in another repository gets from the grill one plain-English question, at the example level and with no model word, for each tried variant that meets every example and prints something else on a step no example takes; a case the owner answers "either output is fine" goes under Not covered.
hyp, the glossary, the spec and both skills say "variant" where they said "switch": select reads variant configs from `specs/variants/`, and its refusal names variant configs.
A commit whose spec folder holds its variant configs under `specs/switches/` is selected or refused as before.
A commit whose spec folder holds no model is selected as before, and hyp runs no model checker and reads no model report.

payload.words: The grill stops trying a variant at its first failed example, and the statechart report counts that failed try as separating the variant.

payload.words: hyp prints the Probe writer's contract, so an agent asked to write an example's Probe follows one stated rule instead of guessing.

lines.text: While a Goal is written or open, hyp status G and hyp status G --role probe-writer print in the probe-writer block the Probe writer's contract, the generic Probe, and one task for each line of the Goal. The contract says: read the line, its example and H0; write and commit only that example's probe folder; start from the generic Probe and write new code only when it cannot run the example; run the example on H0 with hyp try and return its output; write no event.
What hyp status prints for the owner, the grill and the runner, what hyp status with no Goal prints, and the probe-writer block of a selected or landed Goal stay as they are.

payload.words: A grill that follows the hyp-grill skill makes the moves the owner agreed for v2: in the first grill, in the re-grill, and when it tries variants and hands an example to the Probe writer.

lines.text: In a first grill of a written Goal's examples, the grill asks for each line "What would you do, and what would you see?" and makes the owner's answer that line's example, without reading it back for approval; when an answer has two things to see, it warns that the line combines two rules and proposes a split, which the owner decides; it writes the floor from the want, reads the line's "must never" words aloud and asks "What could a wrong build print that this floor still lets through?", and each wrong output the owner names becomes a ceiling; and once every line has an example that gives its line's verdict on H0, it stops asking and says the Goal has enough.

In a re-grill at a stop, when the owner reports something odd, the grill asks the owner to state it as "on input X, I must see Y" or "I must never see Y", and proposes an adjust when a line's words already ask for Y or forbid it, and a new Goal when Y needs new words.

When the grill tries a Goal's variants, it stops trying a variant at its first failed example. When the generic Probe cannot run an example, the grill hands that example to a Probe writer that it starts with what hyp status G prints for the Probe writer, and writes no new Probe code itself; an example the generic Probe can run gets the generic Probe.

payload.words: The grill places a Goal's whole example set with one `hyp place G`, and the set counts only when every example agrees with its line about H0.

lines.text: `hyp place G` places every example under `goals/G/<line>/` in one act, and only when each example agrees with its line about H0: a gap example fails on H0, a guard example is met on H0.
When an example disagrees with its line about H0, `hyp place G` places none of the set and names each example that disagrees, in its line's words.

`hyp place G` places none of the set, and names each cause, when a line holds no example, when an example placed before is missing, when an example is not committed, or when a new version changes more than its floors and ceilings.
A `hyp place G` that changes no example is refused, and only a place that changed the set restarts the budget; a change under `goals/G/specs/` alone is no change.
While the Goal is written or open, the grill's allowed acts show one ready place line, `hyp place G`; the form `hyp place G LINE/EXAMPLE` is refused as a bad argument.
Every Goal recorded before this change keeps the state, stop, runs and allowed acts `hyp status` prints for it.

payload.words: Git keeps only the owner's acts, the place of each example set and the select, while every cell, Result and output stays in the clone's trace as a cache that a reader fills by running an example again, and hyp warns when a selected commit is on no branch or tag.

lines.text: `hyp place G` writes to `.tree/` only one line that names the example set's hashes; H0's cells and outputs go to the clone's trace.
`hyp run` writes nothing under `.tree/`, and `hyp select` writes to `.tree/` only one line that names the commit and the example hashes it was judged by; Results and outputs go to the clone's trace.
In a clone whose trace lacks a cell that `hyp status G` would print, it says the cell is not in this clone's trace and prints the ready `hyp try` line that runs it again.
A `hyp try` of a missing cell saves that cell in the clone's trace, and `hyp status G` then prints it, marked as run again in this clone.

Every state block of a selected or landed Goal (`hyp status`, `hyp status G`, and the return of `hyp select` and `hyp land`) prints a warning when the selected commit is on no branch or tag, also when another commit with the same subject hash is on one.
In a clone whose trace holds no run of an open Goal, `hyp status G` prints `runs: 0 of 3 used`, whatever other clones ran.
`hyp status G` of every landed Goal on main prints as it does on the base.
A runner in a fresh clone of the record branch can run every line of an open Goal and select a candidate met on every line.

payload.words: The owner ends a Goal with land or close, and an ended Goal holds exactly what it held when the owner ended it, in every clone.

lines.text: The owner closes a Goal that is not ended with one act hyp status prints, and status then shows it `ended` with a line naming the close, its actor and time; a close by another role or actor is refused.
A landed Goal shows `ended`, with a line naming the land.

After a land or close, a Result or select written in another clone before it that the end does not name is refused at replay and listed under 'refused at replay', so the ended Goal's rows and verdicts are those the owner saw.
A closed Goal refuses place, run, select, unselect, land and a second close.
`hyp add goal --from G` accepts a closed Goal like a landed one.
Land on a Goal whose runs have not stopped is refused.
A log written before close existed replays with nothing refused, and each Goal keeps its rows and verdicts.

`hyp spec` prints every act's usage line and every refusal code with its exit code, and `hyp help` and each refusal agree with it.
